# Container fixtures

Synthetic vault containers for testing the container layer
(`docs/format/01-container.md`). They were produced with Banking4, so they
show what Banking4 really puts on disk. They contain generated bytes and
made-up names only: no bank data, no real password.

`MANIFEST.json` lists, for every container, the password, the header values
and every entry of the finished file. A test opens each container with the
listed password, walks the tree and compares paths, flags, sizes and SHA-256
digests.

| File | What it is for |
|------|----------------|
| `v01-aes256-c512-r100000.sub` | reference: every content case, 100000 key-stretching rounds |
| `v02-aes256-c512-r0.sub` | the same content with 0 rounds (fast to open) |
| `v03-empty-password.sub` | empty password |
| `v04-aes128-c4096-r1000.sub` | AES-128, 4096-byte clusters, a directory with more than 64 entries |
| `v05-aes192-c1024-r3.sub` | AES-192, 1024-byte clusters, password with non-ASCII and non-BMP characters |
| `v06-flags2-c512-r100000.sub` | security flags value 2, content type of a Banking4 data vault, created while a device GUID was supplied |
| `v07-device-bound-c512-r10.sub` | security flags value 1: needs the device GUID from the manifest |
| `v08-token-c512-r10.sub` | an access token was issued (token and usage string in the manifest) |
| `v09-password-changed-c512-r50000.sub` | password, round count and flags changed after the content was written |

## What is inside

v01 and v02 hold the full set, the others a smaller one. Between them:

- files of 0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32 and 33 bytes, of one cluster minus one
  byte, exactly one cluster, one cluster plus one byte, two clusters, and of
  many clusters (in v01, v02 and v05 long enough to run into the second page
  of the allocation table). Most are encrypted; the sizes at the boundaries
  exist as plain files too;
- nested directories, an empty directory, a directory whose entries fill
  several pages;
- names with non-ASCII characters, names of exactly 54 bytes, and names that
  were longer than 54 bytes when written. Banking4 cuts those at byte 54, in
  two cases in the middle of a character; `name_utf8` in the manifest has the
  stored bytes, `path` the text they read as (with U+FFFD for the broken
  character) and `requested_name` what was asked for;
- files and directories that were deleted again, a file that was replaced by
  a shorter one, files written afterwards into the freed clusters and slots,
  and (v01, v02) free clusters that still hold old data.

## File contents

Byte `i` of the file with seed `k` (the `seed` of its manifest entry) is the
top byte of a 32-bit linear congruential generator:

```
x = (k * 2654435761 + 1) mod 2^32
for each byte:  x = (x * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32;  byte = x >> 24
```

So a test can recompute any file from `seed` and `size` instead of trusting
only the digest.

## Manifest fields

Per container: `file`, `file_size`, `file_sha256` (of the container file, to
detect a manifest that belongs to other files), `password`, `device_guid` (the
GUID that was supplied when the container was created, or null; it is needed
for opening only when bit 0 of the security flags is set, as in v07, and must
make no difference otherwise, as in v06), `requested` (the values the
container was to be created with),
`header` (the values of the finished file), `content_key` (hex; the
fixtures hold no secrets, and it lets key recovery be tested on its own),
optionally `token` and `created_with`, and `entries`.

Per entry, in Banking4's listing order with a directory before its contents:
`path` (the names as Banking4 lists them, joined with `/`),
`kind` (`file` or `dir`), `name_utf8` (hex of the stored name: the UTF-8 form
of the requested name, cut at 54 bytes), `requested_name` where the name was
cut, `size`, `flags` (1 = encrypted, 2 = directory), `encrypted`, and for
files `seed`, `sha256` of
the plaintext and `read_back` (true when the file of the finished container
reads back as exactly these bytes).

## Regenerating

Nothing in this repository builds these files. Do not edit them.

Salts, GUIDs, content keys and timestamps are drawn anew for every container,
so the containers are not byte-for-byte reproducible. The manifest belongs to
exactly these files and always matches them; the two are committed together.
